topic: South Indian Dynasties (Rashtrakutas, Cholas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas, Yadavas)

items.front: Who founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty and when?
items.back: Dantidurga (c.753 CE), by overthrowing the Badami Chalukya Kirtivarman II.
items.examPoint: Rashtrakuta origins — Chalukya feudatories; founder Dantidurga (c.753 CE)

items.front: Which Rashtrakuta king built the monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora?
items.back: Krishna I — carved top-down from a single rock.
items.examPoint: Krishna I — Kailasa (Kailashnatha) rock-cut temple at Ellora

items.front: Rashtrakuta king who moved the capital to Manyakheta and wrote the Kavirajamarga?
items.back: Amoghavarsha I; earliest Kannada poetics; turned to Jainism under Jinasena.
items.examPoint: Amoghavarsha I — Manyakheta capital, Kavirajamarga, conversion to Jainism

items.front: Which Chola inscription records early local self-government, and under whom?
items.back: Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I (c.919/921 CE); kudavolai (pot-ticket) election.
items.examPoint: Chola local self-government — Uttaramerur inscriptions & kudavolai system

items.back: Ur (ordinary revenue-paying), Brahmadeya (tax-free Brahmin grant), Devadana (granted to a temple).
items.examPoint: Chola village types — Ur, Brahmadeya, Devadana

items.front: Which Chola king built the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur?
items.back: Rajaraja I (consecrated 1009-10); also conquered Ceylon and the Maldives.

items.front: Chola king with the title Gangaikonda who led a navy against Srivijaya?
items.back: Rajendra I; defeated Pala king Mahipala, reached the Ganga, raided SE Asia (Sumatra/Java).
items.examPoint: Rajendra I — Gangaikonda title, Ganges & Southeast Asia campaigns

items.front: Which Chola king united the Eastern (Vengi) Chalukyas with the Cholas and abolished tolls?
items.examPoint: Kulottunga I — union of Vengi Chalukyas & Cholas; abolition of tolls

items.front: Name the three UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples and their builders.
items.back: Thanjavur (Rajaraja I), Gangaikondacholapuram (Rajendra I), Airavatesvara/Darasuram (Rajaraja II).
items.examPoint: Great Living Chola Temples (UNESCO World Heritage)

items.front: What is the finest example of Chola lost-wax bronze casting?
items.back: The Nataraja (dancing Shiva); Dravidian style = pyramidal vimana, mandapas, gopura.

items.front: Kakatiya king who built Pakhal Lake and issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam?
items.back: Ganapati Deva; shifted the capital to Warangal (Orugallu).
items.examPoint: Ganapati Deva — Pakhal Lake & Motupalli port (Abhaya Sasanam)

items.front: First woman ruler of the Kakatiyas, praised by Marco Polo?
items.back: Rudrama Devi. Warangal fell to the Tughlaqs in 1323 under Prataparudra II.
items.examPoint: Rudrama Devi — first woman ruler & Marco Polo's account

items.front: Kakatiya monument that became a UNESCO site in 2021?
items.back: Ramappa (Rudreswara) Temple, Palampet; Kakatiyas were famed for tank irrigation.
items.examPoint: Kakatiya legacy — tank irrigation, Ramappa Temple & Telugu literature

items.front: Hoysala king who built Belur & Halebidu; and what ended the dynasty?
items.back: Vishnuvardhana (soapstone, stellate plan); Veera Ballala III died at the Battle of Madurai (1343).
items.examPoint: Hoysalas — Vishnuvardhana, Belur/Halebidu & Hoysala temple style

items.front: Shivaji's council of eight; and the two Maratha levies on outside lands?
items.back: Ashtapradhan (Peshwa = PM); Chauth (1/4) and Sardeshmukhi (extra 1/10) on mulk lands.
items.examPoint: Shivaji's Ashtapradhan — the eight ministers and their portfolios (Peshwa, Amatya, Sachiv, Sumant/Dabir, Senapati, Nyayadhish, Panditrao, Waqia-Navis)
